Issued at 256 AM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

Today-Tonight...An inverted trough across the Bahamas will shift 
westward and across Florida today, ushering in deep tropical 
moisture, with PW values rising to 2.1-2.3". This will lead to high 
rain chances (~70%) today and continue the threat for localized 
heavy rainfall and mostly minor flooding issues across the area. 
Through early this morning, scattered showers and storms across the 
waters will push onshore, with coverage of this activity increasing, 
becoming scattered to numerous with daytime heating. Showers and 
storms will spread westward from the coast and across the interior 
through late morning and into the afternoon/early evening. While 
steering winds strengthen slightly today favoring quicker storm 
motion, high rainfall rates and any repeated rounds of showers and 
storms will easily lead to localized totals of 2-4" (potentially
up to 5" in isolated spots) in a short period of time. This may 
lead to mostly minor nuisance flooding of roadways and poor 
drainage areas. However, should totals toward the higher end of
this range occur, it could lead to isolated flash flooding, mostly
in the form of more significant standing water issues on roadways.

Some pockets of drier air aloft, with DCAPE values of 600-800 J/kg, 
and a slight increase in low to mid level E/SE flow could also lead 
to a few stronger storms producing frequent lightning strikes and 
strong wind gusts to 40-50 mph as they push toward the west-
northwest. Showers, storms and lingering areas of debris cloud 
rainfall will diminish into the evening across the interior. 
However, low level SE winds will still be able to transport isolated 
to scattered showers and storms onshore, continuing low end rain 
chances (20-30%) along the coast overnight. 

Considerable cloud cover, onshore winds and higher convective 
coverage will keep highs near to a tad below normal in the upper 80s 
to around 90 degrees. However, the moist airmass will lead to very 
humid conditions, which will still lead to peak heat index values up 
to 100-105F. Warm and muggy conditions will continue into tonight, 
with lows in the 70s. 

At the beaches, a building swell and a moderate onshore breeze will 
lead to a High Risk of rip currents at area beaches today that will 
likely continue into Saturday. 

Saturday-Sunday...As inverted trough shifts west, deep moisture (PW 
2.0-2.3") will linger across the area Saturday, continuing high rain 
chances up to 60-70%. Greatest coverage of showers and storms looks 
to focus across the interior as Atlantic ridge axis north of the 
area keeps an onshore flow across the region. Typical summer-time 
storm threats persist with isolated stronger storms capable of 
producing strong wind gusts to 50 mph and frequent lightning. The 
moist airmass and a weakening of steering winds will also continue 
(and may even slightly enhance) the threat for locally heavy 
rainfall of 2-4" and potential for mostly minor flooding. Into 
Sunday, deeper moisture shifts north-northwest, as mid level ridge 
across the Atlantic begins to extend westward across Florida. This 
results in a slight decline in rain chances into late weekend, but 
scattered coverage of showers and storms are still forecast into the 
afternoon/evening (PoPs of 30-50%). An increase in dry air aloft 
will continue the threat for some stronger storms Sunday. Convection 
will wind down each evening this weekend, with mostly dry conditions 
forecast overnight. 

Highs will rise slightly into the weekend, but still be close to 
normal, in the low 90s for most locations. However, max temps in the 
mid 90s may return northwest of I-4 on Sunday afternoon. As humid 
conditions persist, peak heat index values will also climb, ranging 
from 102-107F for much of the area. Lows will continue to range from 
the mid to upper 70s. 

Monday-Thursday...Atlantic ridge axis shifts back south across the 
area into early next week, and then slowly shifts farther south of 
the area by mid to late week as a frontal trough pushes into the 
Southeast United States. This will gradually veer low level winds 
from the southeast Monday to the south-southeast Tuesday and then 
out of the west-southwest Wednesday into Thursday. However, winds 
remain weak and the east coast sea breeze will still form and move 
inland each day. Mid level ridge shifts westward across the state 
and remains firmly in place through much of next week. This combined 
with advection of drier air will lead to lower than normal rain 
chances into next week. Forecast PoPs are currently no more than 20-
30% for each afternoon/evening. With coverage of showers and storms 
remaining isolated to scattered each day and with ridge in place, 
temperatures will continue to rise, with highs in the low to mid 90s 
each day. Will have to monitor for any Heat Advisories as peak heat 
index values may have the potential to rise to 108-110 in some 
spots.
